answer: Sybil resistance can be a scarce, address-bound delay rather than a name check. Each identity must finish a ferrous-hard verifiable delay, keyed to its own address and the epoch seed, before it may vote or grade. That proof cannot be copied onto other keys, so a farm pays wall-clock time for every shell. After peers verify the proofs, rewards move like a river only through accounts that also posted original work. Cloned shells never taste that nectar: reused proofs fail the address bind, and late proofs miss the window.
